scenario.name: r-cd-return-covenant-authority
scenario.description: Return-covenant authority must survive a real gateway restart. The recipient session's authority generation (the session_recipient_authority epoch) must stay present and unchanged at every sample, including the outage where no process serves, and the transition's bodies and the replacement's output must be retained rather than lost. A generation is usable only while it owns the listener, /readyz passes and hello-ok answers; an unchanged epoch alone is not usability, and continuous service across a restart is not asserted (at F′ the old server closes before any successor is ready). The outage is measured and reported as outageInterval. Four cases: the positive on the supervised branch (the one systemd-supervised fleet seats take), the external-supervisor negative (port held; that branch has no in-process fallback), and two spawned-branch negatives on an unmanaged gateway restarted with update.run: negative-spawned-fallback (the product-spawned child never serves; the original process must reacquire and serve again, which is old-process restoration, not fresh-successor proof) and negative-spawned-runtime-unavailable (the product refuses the fallback because its child runtime is gone).
scenario.notes: Fixture-gated: k6 cannot start, observe or replace a gateway, so the k6 entry fails closed and the executable control is scripts/run-return-covenant-restart-control.mjs (see the product-path map, with F′ path:line anchors, in scenarios/r-cd-return-covenant-authority.js). The control owns the lifecycle of one disposable gateway that composite-launcher.sh set up and then stopped. For positive and negative-replacement-never-usable it is the declared external supervisor (OPENCLAW_SUPERVISOR_MODE=external), so the restart takes the supervised branch (src/cli/gateway-cli/run-loop.ts:497-561), the branch systemd-supervised fleet seats take. For the two spawned negatives it sets no supervisor hint at all (read back from the old generation's /proc environ) and requests the restart with reason update.run, so F′ takes the spawned branch (respawnGatewayProcessForUpdate, run-loop.ts:459-495); restartGatewayProcessWithFreshPid never spawns (src/infra/process-respawn.ts:231-273). It refuses any target that is not $HOME/proof-gw/comp-<sha8> with a matching receipts/identity.json, a stopped openclaw-proof-comp-<sha8> unit, a free loopback port that is not the live gateway's, no channels, and a stage whose dist/build-info.json commit is the candidate. Grading, from the signed record only: PASS-candidate needs all five receipts plus the positive behaviour (old generation ready before the transition; restart accepted; old exits 0 through an accepted full-process external handoff bound to its PID; every sample shows the same authority epoch; the old generation observed serving before the transition and the replacement observed serving from its first serving sample to the end of the window, serving meaning it owns the listener while /readyz passes and hello-ok answers; replacement ready within the deadline with a new PID, socket inode and bootId, both generations reporting the staged buildId; full planned window observed without blind gaps; clean docs harness; cleanup left nothing running). FAIL-candidate when the behaviour is contradicted: authority cleared or advanced, old generation not serving before the transition, no handoff, replacement never serving or not staying served, generations not distinct, or residue after cleanup. Every receipt reports outageInterval (last serving old sample to first serving sample after it, in ms, at one-sample resolution); it is reported, not graded against a bound. MISSING-candidate when there is nothing to judge: no observation matrix, no established authority, or a restart that was never accepted (its failure body is still kept). PARTIAL-candidate when the restart was observed uncontradicted but a receipt or bound is missing (lost transition body, process output, fingerprint, unsigned cleanup, unreadable authority sample, short window, dirty harness). negative-replacement-never-usable holds the port with a control-owned socket before the control starts the replacement; it must grade non-PASS with the epoch, the old fingerprint and the failure body retained and noFallback (that branch has none). negative-spawned-fallback holds the port from the old listener's close until the product-spawned child is gone; it must grade non-PASS with negativeControl.holds: the child never served, the product's 'did not become healthy ... falling back to in-process restart' line and the restart frame are retained, the original PID and start ticks own the listener again with /readyz and hello-ok passing, the epoch is unchanged, and outageInterval is measured. That is old-process restoration, never fresh-successor proof and never PASS. negative-spawned-runtime-unavailable runs the old generation on a control-owned runtime copy and removes it before the transition; the product must name child-runtime-unavailable and exit nonzero. Named non-PASS fallback branches, from the product's own diagnostic: require-fresh-process, child-runtime-unavailable, foreground-closed, installation-replaced and resources-retained grade a limit (the old runtime is not viable, or was replaced, so the fallback's precondition is false); lock-reacquire-failed grades a failure. A limit alone grades MISSING-candidate, a failure FAIL-candidate; neither is ever PASS, and no negative case can grade PASS. The only earlier attempt (historical-baseline-review: zero of 24 observations, no signed cleanup/observer receipt) is not evidence.
scenario.registryNotes: Ledger command AUTHORITY-RESTART-CONTROL, gate reviewed-restart-control-on-final-successor. Rejected base: the first gateway-restart transition cleared the current generation before the replacement became usable, and the exact failure body was lost. The row stays required and MISSING at F′ until this control runs on the final successor (🌊, Discord msg 1565895695586558120). 🌊's ruling on the fork (Discord msg 1565903655885082677): the spawned branch closes the old server before the child's readiness, so continuous old-process service is not an invariant; the never-usable negative proves the narrower fallback, and a blocked fallback is a failure or limit, not PASS.

invocation.transition: gateway.restart.request {reason: gateway.restart, skipDeferral: true} with operator.admin on the supervised cases; {reason: update.run, skipDeferral: true} on the spawned cases (the untargeted request passes its reason to the run loop; no update is performed)
invocation.authority: sessions.create then session.visibility.set(suggest); the narrowing advances session_recipient_authority
invocation.supervisor: positive and negative-replacement-never-usable: OPENCLAW_SUPERVISOR_MODE=external, and the control consumes the restart handoff and starts the replacement; spawned cases: no supervisor hint, the product spawns and judges the replacement
invocation.fixtureState: an existing proof-gw directory (composite-launcher.sh setup, then stop); its state is kept for composite-launcher.sh shred

expectedReceipts.name: transition-http-body
expectedReceipts.description: The gateway.restart.request response frame (private verbatim, public redacted, SHA-256 of the canonical frame), plus the /readyz and /startupz bodies at the transition edges: the last pre-transition body, the first not-ready body (draining 503 or refused), the replacement's first ready body, and the last not-ready body when no replacement serves. The rejected base lost the failure body.

expectedReceipts.name: replacement-process-output
expectedReceipts.description: The replacement's stdout and stderr, captured by the control as its supervisor: byte counts and SHA-256 in public with a redacted tail, raw logs in the private directory. A replacement that never serves keeps them as the failure text. On the spawned branch the product starts the child with inherited stdio (src/infra/process-respawn.ts:295-299), so its output is in the old generation's streams; the control keeps those, plus every restart diagnostic line (the product's fallback and refusal lines, the child's bind failure) redacted in fallback.diagnostics.

expectedReceipts.name: generation-fingerprints
expectedReceipts.description: Old and replacement process fingerprints (PID, kernel start ticks), each one's listening socket inode and port read from /proc, and the hello-ok bootId SHA-256 and buildId. A replacement that never listened keeps its PID and start ticks. On the spawned branch: the product-spawned child's PID, parent PID and start ticks from /proc (or its PID from the product's own diagnostic, 'unknown' when its spawn failed), and, when the original process serves again, its new listening socket inode and bootId under the same PID and start ticks.

expectedReceipts.name: observation-record
expectedReceipts.description: The observation window planned before the transition (sample interval, pre-transition samples, transition, readiness and window bounds, maximum sample gap) and the matrix: per sample the phase, the listener owner, inode, owner PID and start ticks, /readyz and /startupz status with a body SHA-256, hello-ok with a bootId SHA-256, the generation observed serving (owner of the listener while /readyz passes and hello-ok answers), and the authority epoch SHA-256. The grade derives outageInterval from it. The baseline attempt produced zero of twenty-four.

expectedReceipts.name: signed-cleanup-receipt
expectedReceipts.description: Cleanup stops only processes this run started (PID, start ticks and run marker re-verified before any signal), closes the negative's socket, and records that no run process or listener remains. The whole observer receipt is HMAC-SHA256-signed (hmac-sha256-proof-observer-key-v1) with a launcher-held key that the gateway processes never receive. The baseline attempt produced none.

review.notes: The control writes a candidate receipt only. Folding it is a reviewed corpus step on the final successor product. The row is not promoted by this manifest and stays MISSING at F′.

liveRunSafety.notes: run-proof.sh and run-proofs.sh refuse orchestration-required rows, so a catalog or live-suite run never fires this control. An operator runs the fixture against a stopped proof-gw gateway: positive case, then the negative. The fixture never reads OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_TOKEN or OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_WS; it takes the disposable gateway's own token from the proof-gw config. It never restarts, stops or signals a live gateway or any process it did not start.
